extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and interested parties interacting with the South African Patent Office
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing filing, prosecution, recording of interests, PCT national-phase entry, fees, agent registration, and contested proceedings under the South African Patents Act and Patent Regulations (1978).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and joinder by third parties (Form P15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who may wish to become a party to the proceedings may, within two months of the date of the notification or date advertisement in the journal or within any such extended period as may be allowed by the registrar file a reply on Form P15, accompanied by the relevant documents. Form P15 and the relevant documents shall be served on the other party in the matter and proof of service furnished to the satisfaction of the registrar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of Form P15 and the documents shall be served upon any party involved and proof of service furnished to the satisfaction of the registrar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar may determine matter after reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply has been filed or the period for filing thereof has expired and a reply has not been filed, the registrar may appoint a time and date for himself to determine the matter and notify the parties of the time and date thus appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of assignments (Form P16) and proof of title
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for the recording of an assignment shall be made in duplicate on Form P16 accompanied by proof of title of such assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such application shall be made within six months of the event entitling the applicant to request a recording: Provided that the registrar may extend this time limit if so requested on Form P4, and on payment of the prescribed fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and lodging of writs/attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: A warrant or writ of execution or an attachment order in respect of a patent application or a patent shall be served at the address for service of the applicant or the patentee and a copy shall be lodged with the registrar on Form P16 for recording in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entry of any attachment may be removed from the register on a request made to the registrar on Form P4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of licences (Form P16) and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An application to record a licence against a patent shall be made on Form P16 within six months of the event entitling the recording of such licence, or within six months of the grant of the patent, if the licence agreement was before such grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar may extend time limit on application on Form P4 and payment of the prescribed fee. Recording of a licence may be cancelled on request to the registrar on Form P4 accompanied by proof, to the satisfaction of the registrar, that the licence has been cancelled or otherwise terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and removal of hypothecation
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The hypothecation of a patent application shall be recorded in the register on application on Form P16 accompanied by the deed of hypothecation. (2) The application shall also be served on the applicant or the patentee, as the case may be, and any other person recorded in the patent, and proof of service shall be furnished to the satisfaction of the registrar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recording of the hypothecation may be removed from the register on application to the registrar on Form P4, accompanied by such proof of the termination of the hypothecation as the registrar may require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement or cancellation of 'licences of right' endorsement (Form P4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for the endorsement or the cancellation of an endorsement of the words 'licences of right', in terms of sections 53 and 54 of the Act, shall be made on Form P4 within two months after the date giving rise to such endorsement or cancellation thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary surrender of a patent (Form P21)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for the surrender of a patent shall be made on Form P21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office obligations for international (PCT) applications — fees (reg 67A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of section 43C(a), and subject to rule 16bis of the PCT regulations, the applicant shall pay to the patent office the transmittal fee specified in Schedule 1 within one month of the date on which the international application was lodged; and the international fee and the search fee specified in PCT rules 15 and 16 within the time limits specified therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase entry — Form P25 and fees (reg 67B)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The national fee prescribed in section 43E(1)(a) shall be paid by the applicant on Form P25, in duplicate, one copy of which shall be returned by the Registrar to the applicant as proof of payment. (2) The translation referred to in section 43E(1)(b) shall be lodged within six months of the date of lodgement of Form P25. (3) Within one month of complying with sections 43E(1)(a), the applicant shall lodge Form P2. (4) Within six months of complying with section 43E(1)(a), or within such further time as the Registrar may on request allow, the applicant shall lodge Form P3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations, fee payments and subsequent forms P2/P3 have specified time windows; registrar may allow further time on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase entry time limits under PCT Chapter I (reg 67C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Republic has not, before the expiration of 19 months from the priority date, been elected for international preliminary examination: (a) the time limit applicable under article 22 shall be 31 months from the priority date; (b) the contents of the translation shall include the description, the claims (if amended under article 19) and any textual matter on the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase entry time limits under PCT Chapter II (reg 67D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Republic has, before expiration of 19 months from priority date, been elected for international preliminary examination: (a) the time limit applicable under article 39 shall be 31 months from the priority date; (b) the translation shall include the description (if amended by any amendments annexed to the international preliminary examination report), the claims (if so amended), and any textual matter on the drawings (if amended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing translation of an amendment (reg 67E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant fails to file a translation of an amendment referred to in regulation 67C or 67D, the registrar shall request the applicant to furnish the missing translation within a time limit which shall be reasonable in the circumstances and which shall be fixed in the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of agent and applicable time limits (reg 67F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations 9 and 10 shall apply to section 43F(3)(a)(ii) and the prescribed time referred to in section 43F(3)(a)(ii) shall be six months calculated from the date on which the applicant complies with the requirements of section 43E(1), or such further period as the registrar may on request allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention application — priority document and translations (reg 67G)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Where the applicant has failed to comply with rule 17.1 of the PCT regulations, the applicant shall lodge with the patent office a copy, certified to the satisfaction of the registrar, of the priority document within six months of complying with section 43E(1) or within such further period as the registrar may allow. (2) If the priority document is in a language other than English, a translation into one of the official languages, verified to the satisfaction of the registrar, shall be lodged within six months or within such further period as the registrar may allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance, publication and sealing applicability to national phase (reg 67H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to section 40, when read with section 43F(h), sections 42 and 44 and regulations 44 and 47 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the national phase of an international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewals for patents arising from PCT applications (reg 67I)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If a patent issues on an application filed in terms of section 43 three months or more before the expiration of 36 months from the international filing date, regulation 48 shall apply. (2) If a patent issues after the expiration of 36 months or less than three months prior to such expiration, the patentee shall pay any renewal fees payable in terms of regulation 48(1) within six months of the date of publication in terms of section 42 or such further period as the registrar may allow. Thereafter regulation 48 shall apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of patent agents and patent attorneys (reg 68)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be kept at the office a register wherein shall be entered the full names, business addresses and dates of registration of all patent agents and patent attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The register kept under earlier regulations is deemed to form part of this register (reg 69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for registration as patent agent/attorney (Form P17) (reg 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application to be registered as a patent agent or a patent attorney shall be made on Form P17 and shall be accompanied by evidence, to the satisfaction of the registrar, that the applicant is entitled to be so registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the registrar is satisfied he shall enter the name on the register and issue a certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal from register — Form P18 and service requirements (reg 72)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A request for removal from the register of the name of a patent agent or a patent attorney in terms of section 23(1)(a) shall be made on Form P18 and the applicant shall provide proof, to the satisfaction of the registrar, that a copy of that form has been served on the South African Institute of Intellectual Property Law and on the law society concerned. If no objection is received within two weeks the registrar shall remove the name. (2) If the Institute or law society gives notice of intention to be heard, it shall serve notice and documents on the person concerned and registrar. (3) The registrar shall appoint a time and date for the hearing and advise all parties accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension/removal proceedings for agents/attorneys (reg 73)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) An application by the registrar for the suspension from practice or the removal of the name of a person from the register shall be commenced by motion proceedings and copies of all relevant documents shall be served on the person concerned, the SA Institute of IP Law and the law society concerned. (2) An application by the SA Institute of IP Law likewise shall be by motion and served on the registrar and the law society. (3) Thereafter procedure shall be governed by the Uniform Rules of Court of the Supreme Court of South Africa, 1965.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment after removal or suspension (reg 74)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A patent agent or patent attorney whose name has been removed or suspended and who wishes to be employed in any capacity connected with the profession shall lodge an application on Form P4, accompanied by the prescribed fee and evidence on affidavit of circumstances and present character and behaviour. Such application shall be served on the SA Institute of IP Law; if no objection within one month the registrar may decide the matter in the absence of the Institute. (2) An agent who wishes to employ a removed/suspended person shall lodge an application on Form P4 with similar requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of representation rights for attorneys (reg 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney who wishes to continue, after 1 January 1984, to have rights of representation without registration as a patent attorney may apply to the registrar for an extension of such rights on Form P4. The application shall be accompanied by evidence on affidavit of activities in the past five years representing parties in matters under the Act, and of activities and preparation to become registered, together with proof of service on the SA Institute of IP Law and the law society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings before the Commissioner of Patents — permitted initiations (reg 76)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings before the commissioner may be initiated by way of: (a) a notice of appeal; (b) a notice of opposition; (c) an application for revocation; (d) an application for extension of term; (e) a notice of motion; (f) summons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon initiation the registrar shall open a separate file for that proceeding (reg 77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons of registrar — request for written grounds (reg 78)
rubrics_metrics.description: When any person objects to any order or decision of the registrar he may, within one month of the date of the registrar's order or decision or such further time as the registrar may allow, on Form P4 request the registrar to state in writing the grounds for his decision and the data used by him in arriving thereat. The date of such statement shall be deemed to be the date of the registrar's order or decision for the purpose of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Commissioner — lodging and content (regs 79-81)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal shall be lodged with the registrar of the Court of the Commissioner of Patents and served on the registrar and any other party within two months of the statement referred to in reg 78. Any notice of appeal shall be accompanied by a copy of the reasons of the registrar and shall be in accordance with Rule 49(4) of the Uniform Rules of Court. Procedure on appeal shall, as far as practicable, follow provisions governing appeals to the full Court: the record on appeal shall include the registrar's statement, documents containing data used by him and any other documents the appellant considers relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure — Form P19 and timelines (regs 82-88)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of opposition shall be made on Form P19 and accompanied by a statement of particulars of the grounds. Within two months of filing and service the applicant shall file a counterstatement in the form of a plea; failure to do so within the period (or extension) shall deem the application abandoned. Within two months of the counterstatement the opponent shall file evidence by affidavit; within two months of that the applicant may file answering evidence by affidavit; within two months opponent may file replying evidence confined to matters strictly in reply. No further evidence except by leave; all evidence by affidavit unless otherwise directed. Upon completion of evidence, parties may request hearing date (opponent or, if he fails within six weeks, applicant may request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for revocation — Form P20 and timelines (regs 89-94)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for revocation shall be made on Form P20 and accompanied by a statement of particulars of the grounds. Within two months of lodging and service the patentee shall lodge a counterstatement in the form of a plea; if no plea within two months (or extension) the patent shall be deemed to be revoked. Timetable for evidence mirrors opposition: applicant files evidence within two months of counterstatement; patentee files answering evidence within two months; replying evidence within two months; no further evidence except by leave; all evidence by affidavit unless directed. Upon completion of evidence the applicant, or if he fails within six weeks the opponent may request a hearing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reg 94A: If by consent patentee offers to surrender or patent is deemed revoked, registrar when deciding costs shall consider whether proceedings might have been avoided if reasonable notice had been given to the patentee before application was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of future proceedings (Form P22) (reg 95)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may apply by lodging Form P22 in duplicate with the registrar for notice to be given to him of the taking of any action or proceedings in connection with a patent or patent application. As soon as possible after such action or proceeding is taken and, in the case of an application to make an entry, before such entry is made, the registrar shall give notice of such action or proceeding or entry to such person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence applications — service and mode (reg 96)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a compulsory licence under section 55 or 56(1) of the Act shall be brought by way of notice of motion and shall be served on the patentee and any other person who appears from the registrar to have an interest in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of motion — non-resident respondent timeline (reg 97)
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings initiated by notice of motion a party resident or incorporated outside the Republic shall have one month from the date of service of such notice on him within which to lodge and serve his notice of intention to oppose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings for infringement — damages or reasonable royalty enquiries (reg 98)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) In proceedings for infringement where the plaintiff claims relief by way of damages or payment in lieu, it is permissible to claim an enquiry as to the damages suffered and/or what is a reasonable royalty. (2) A plaintiff claiming such an enquiry need not specify in pleadings the amount of damages or the manner of computation. (3) If parties cannot agree on further pleadings, discovery, inspection or other procedural matters relating to the enquiry, either party may make application to the commissioner for directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits (reg 99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits specified may be extended by consent of the parties or, failing such consent, by the registrar on a request made to him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tariff of fees for proceedings before commissioner and registrar (reg 100)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tariff of fees applicable to proceedings before the commissioner and the registrar shall be those applicable for the time being in a Provincial Division of the Supreme Court in terms of the Uniform Rules of Court: Provided that (a) fees allowed to a patent agent or patent attorney may be allowed on the same scale as that allowed to junior counsel for work connected with appearances without counsel; (b) in allowing a fee for perusal and drafting of complex technical documents, the registrar may increase the fees, at his discretion, by a percentage related to the technical complexities of any matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must be paid before or at time of doing the matter (Schedule 1 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following fees shall be paid in connection with applications, registrations and other matters under the Act. Such fees must in all cases be paid before or at the time of doing the matter in respect of which they are to be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific filing and renewal fees (Schedule 1 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule 1 lists applicable fees for many actions (e.g., application for a patent accompanied by a provisional specification R60; complete specification R590; various fees for late claiming of priority, inspection, extensions, corrections, restorations, renewals per year, recording transactions, agent registration, oppositions, revocation applications, PCT transmittal, international and search fees, and national PCT fees as enumerated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule provides year-by-year renewal fee schedule and itemised fees for many formal actions; specific values and items must be consulted in Schedule 1 (many entries and amounts given). Some items reference substitutions by later Government Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT/EPO/AU/US search & designation fees and currency equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule 1 lists PCT-related fees and equivalent currency amounts for offices (e.g., EPO, Australia, United States) and indicates basic fee, supplement per sheet over 30, designation fee, PCT-EASY reduction, search fee, and fee for priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National fee in terms of section 43E(1)(a) (Form P25) and amounts for EPO/AU/US are enumerated with ZAR equivalents in schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form P1 contents and attachments (Schedule 2 — Form P1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form P1 (Application for a patent and acknowledgement of receipt) must include applicant name/reference, title of invention, priority claim (country, number, date), whether patent of addition or fresh application, and be accompanied by specified documents (e.g., provisional or complete specification copies, drawings, publication particulars and abstract (Form P8), copy of priority documents, translations, assignments, declaration and power of attorney (Form P3), request for ante-dating Form P4, etc.). Applicants must have address for service in the Republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate returned as proof of lodging but not valid unless endorsed with official stamp. Attention drawn to regulations 34-37 and that fees are payable per Schedule 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form P2 Register fields (Schedule 2 — Form P2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form P2 contains register fields for provisional/complete lodging dates, acceptance/granted dates, international classification, full names of applicants/patentees/inventors, priority claimed, title of invention, address for service, amendments and rectifications, proceedings before commissioner, licences/attachments/hypothecations, renewals, restorations, court proceedings, and remarks for office use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and power of attorney (Form P3) — required statement (Schedule 2 — Form P3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form P3 is the required Declaration and Power of Attorney under section 30 and regulations 8, 22(1)(c) and 33. It contains the declarant's affirmation that they are the applicant(s) or authorized and have knowledge of the facts stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form P3 must accompany applications where required and follows the regulation references noted.
